item.title: Navatu Secondary U19 team creates history but the job is not over
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 19/08/2026 The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has created history as the first northern team to book a place in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final, but the job is not yet over.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 19/08/2026

The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has created history as the first northern team to book a place in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final, but the job is not yet over.

Speaking to the players after their historic win over Ratu Kadavulevu School last weekend, head coach Alipate Ravulo says they had achieved what they had set out to do and should now be ready for the next challenge.

He says they should always stay grounded and start from zero again, rather than putting themselves on a pedestal.

Ravulo adds that nothing has changed in terms of the goal they want to achieve.

He also acknowledged the hard work and determination shown by the players, as well as the support from their parents and the Vanua.

A new champion will be crowned in the Under-19 grade after defending champions Nasinu Secondary School fell to Ratu Navula College 30-25 in the quarter-final.

Navatu Secondary School will face Lelean Memorial School at 2.20pm at the HFC Bank Stadium.

In the other Deans finals, Ratu Navula College will take on QVS at 8am in the Under-14 grade, followed by RKS facing Marist Brothers High School in the Under-15 grade at 9.05am.

Suva Grammar School will meet RKS at 12.50pm in the Under-17 grade, while Grammar will face Lelean at 6.10pm in the Under-18 grade.

In the Weet-Bix Raluve finals, Nasinu Secondary School will play Saint Vincent College at 10.25am, while Lomary Secondary School will meet MGM High School at 5.05pm.

All games will be played at the HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Grammar dominates Vodafone Super Deans finals with three title showdowns
item.description: Suva Grammar School dominates the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans finals this week, featuring in the Under-16, Under-17 and main Under-18 finals. The Grammar Under-18 team set the benchmark in last week’s semi-final, outclassing Ra High School 51-0.
item.content:encoded:
Suva Grammar School dominates the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans finals this week, featuring in the Under-16, Under-17 and main Under-18 finals.

The Grammar Under-18 team set the benchmark in last week’s semi-final, outclassing Ra High School 51-0.

They dominated both the forwards and backlines, sending a strong message to their opponents that they will not be easy to beat in this week’s final.

In the Under-16 grade, Grammar will face Queen Victoria School at 11.30am, while in the Under-17 division, Grammar will meet Ratu Kadavulevu School at 12.50pm, while in the Under 18, Grammar plays Lelean at 6.10pm.

In the Under-14 grade, QVS will meet Ratu Navula College at 8am.

At 9.05am RKS will face Marist Brothers High School i n the Under-15 grade.

In the Raluve Under-16, Nasinu Secondary School plays Saint Vincent College at 10.25am.

At 2.20pm Lelean will face Navatu Secondary School in the Under-19 grade.

In the Under-18 Raluve, Lomary High School will meet Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School at 5.05pm.

All games will be played at the HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Taveuni students make sacrifices to chase national netball success in Suva
item.description: After fundraising and receiving strong support from their parents, four Holy Cross College netball teams have made the journey from Taveuni to Suva with hopes of taking national titles back home. Holy Cross College teacher and coach Viliame Waqalevu says the school has brought its Under-14 girls, Under-15 girls, Open girls and Open boys teams to compete in the Fiji Secondary Schools Netball nation
item.content:encoded:
After fundraising and receiving strong support from their parents, four Holy Cross College netball teams have made the journey from Taveuni to Suva with hopes of taking national titles back home.

Holy Cross College teacher and coach Viliame Waqalevu says the school has brought its Under-14 girls, Under-15 girls, Open girls and Open boys teams to compete in the Fiji Secondary Schools Netball national tournament.

Waqalevu says one of their biggest challenges was raising enough money to travel from Taveuni to Suva.

He says the students carried out a number of fundraising activities and also contributed towards their travel expenses, while parents provided strong support to make the trip possible.

Holy Cross will be aiming for more national success, particularly through its Open girls team, which Waqalevu says has won the national title for the past two years.

He says their main goal is to defend the Open girls title and win the Under-14 competition, while they are also hoping for strong performances from their Under-15 girls and Open boys teams.

This is Waqavlevu's first year at Holy Cross College after spending the past five years teaching in the Western Division, and it is also his first time bringing the school teams to the national tournament in Suva.

He is calling on families and supporters from Taveuni who are in Suva to come out and support the students.

The national tournament will be held at Jai Narayan College, with the matchups and playing times expected to be confirmed following the AGM this afternoon.

item.title: 56 teams ready for Fiji Secondary School Soccer battle in Labasa
item.description: Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 19/08/2026 The Fiji Secondary School Soccer Championship kicks off today at Subrail Park and other school grounds around Labasa, with 56 teams set to compete for top honours.
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 19/08/2026

The Fiji Secondary School Soccer Championship kicks off today at Subrail Park and other school grounds around Labasa, with 56 teams set to compete for top honours.

Senior Executive Officer Mohammed Shaid says teams will compete in the Under-15 Boys, Under-17 Boys, Under-19 Boys and Open Girls divisions.

Shaid says excitement is building in Labasa, with teams from around Viti Levu arriving in the Northern town since Monday.

He says Labasa is expected to be busy over the weekend as hundreds of students, coaches and supporters gather for the tournament.

Meanwhile, Nakasi High School Open Grade Girls coach Vimlesh Lal says his team is ready for the challenge stressing this is the first time the Nakasi High girls have travelled to Labasa for the competition, and it will be a valuable learning experience for the players.

He says the team played several preparation matches before travelling north to build confidence and prepare for different opponents .

Lal says their main aim is to bring the title back to Nakasi High School, adding that the school has been waiting for a long time to win the championship.

The Fiji Secondary School Soccer Championship will be from today till Saturday in Labasa, with schools from across Fiji battling for the title.

item.title: Tabuya opens Kadavu Rugby doors to Deans finalists
item.description: Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change and the first-ever female President of a Rugby Union in Fiji, Lynda Tabuya, says the doors of the Kadavu Rugby Union are open to players participating in this week’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final if they are interested in joining the team. Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Tabuya says Deans players who want to c
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Information, Environment and Climate Change and the first-ever female President of a Rugby Union in Fiji, Lynda Tabuya, says the doors of the Kadavu Rugby Union are open to players participating in this week’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final if they are interested in joining the team.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Tabuya says Deans players who want to continue developing their rugby careers can join Kadavu Rugby Union for valuable exposure and game experience.

She is also looking forward to an exciting Super Deans final between Suva Grammar School and Lelean Memorial School.

Tabuya says she is proud of both teams for reaching the final, particularly Suva Grammar, which has been chasing Deans glory for a long time.

She says she is backing Lelean Memorial School in the Under-18 final, given the school’s connection to the Triple N Zone and the fact that several members of her family attended the school.

Tabuya wishes all players taking part in the finals this week the best and hopes to see a good display of tough clean and competitive rugby.

Lelean will face Grammar in the grand final of the Vodafone Super Deans this Saturday at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.
